papers.title: Determinants influencing triage system at tertiary care centre as perceived by triage nurse: a qualitative study.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study is to explore the lived experiences of triage nurses.
papers.summary: This qualitative study explores the lived experiences of triage nurses at a tertiary care center to identify factors that influence the triage system. The findings highlight key determinants such as workload, communication, and institutional support, which affect triage accuracy and efficiency. These insights can inform improvements in triage protocols and nursing support.

papers.title: Diabetic Hyperglycemia Induces Region-Specific Transcriptomic Remodeling in the Cochlea.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is associated with sensorineural hearing loss, but the cochlear molecular alterations related to this complication remain unclear. This pilot study aimed to characterize auditory function and region-specific transcriptomic changes in the diabetic cochlea.
papers.summary: This pilot study investigates how diabetic hyperglycemia affects the cochlea at the molecular level, revealing region-specific transcriptomic changes that may underlie diabetes-associated hearing loss. The findings provide initial insights into the gene expression remodeling in different cochlear regions under diabetic conditions.

papers.title: AMIUgraph: analysis and modeling of interactions for utility-driven benchmarking of graph-based models in healthcare.
papers.abstract: Graph-based machine learning approaches, including Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) methods and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), have emerged as powerful tools for modeling complex biomedical data. However, a systematic and clinically grounded comparison of these approaches across heterogeneous healthcare graphs, accounting for both predictive performance and real-world deployment constraints, is still lacking.
papers.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
papers.summary: This paper introduces AMIUgraph, a framework for benchmarking graph-based machine learning models in healthcare, focusing on utility-driven evaluation that accounts for both predictive performance and real-world deployment constraints. It provides a systematic comparison of Knowledge Graph Embedding and Graph Neural Network methods across heterogeneous healthcare graphs.

papers.title: ViBioChain: a blockchain-enabled architecture for privacy-preserving, ethically governed, and explainable personalized gene editing.
papers.abstract: Personalized gene editing demands robust mechanisms for privacy, ethical governance, and verifiable data integrity. This paper proposes ViBioChain, a modular blockchain-anchored architecture integrating five components: (1) differential chain-of-custody audit combining quantum fingerprinting with post-quantum signatures for immutable genomic audit trails; (2) proof-of-bioethical-compliance employing zero-knowledge proofs and AI-based ontology evaluation for automated bioethical gating; (3) federated genomic trust mesh (FGTM) enabling privacy-preserving collaborative model training with Renyi d
papers.summary: ViBioChain is a proposed blockchain-based architecture that aims to make personalized gene editing more privacy-preserving, ethically governed, and explainable. It integrates components like quantum fingerprinting, zero-knowledge proofs, and federated learning to address data integrity, bioethical compliance, and collaborative model training, though it is a conceptual framework rather than a validated implementation.

papers.title: Ontology-driven energy-efficient SAID framework for 5G and IoT networks using cryptographic techniques.
papers.abstract: The rapid deployment and usage of 5G and IoT networks in smart cities present significant challenges for cybersecurity, particularly regarding energy efficiency and attack detection. Existing intrusion detection systems often fail to balance high detection accuracy with low energy consumption, especially in resource-constrained environments. This research paper proposes an ontology-driven novel computational framework for energy-efficient Security Attack Identification and Detection (SAID) in 5G and IoT networks. The research framework proposed is a combination of cryptographic algorithms and
papers.summary: This paper proposes an ontology-driven framework for energy-efficient security attack identification and detection (SAID) in 5G and IoT networks, combining cryptographic algorithms to balance high detection accuracy with low energy consumption. The framework addresses the challenge of intrusion detection in resource-constrained smart city environments.

papers.title: A haplotype-resolved, chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for Carya glabra (pignut hickory; Juglandaceae).
papers.abstract: Carya glabra (2n = 4x = 64), also known as pignut hickory, is a widely distributed species in the walnut family (Juglandaceae). Native to the central and eastern United States and southeastern Canada, C. glabra plays an important ecological role as a common upland forest species; it is closely related to several economically valuable nut trees, including Carya illinoinensis (pecan). A deeper understanding of the genetics of C. glabra is essential for studying its evolutionary history and biology, with potential implications for agricultural improvement of pecan. Here, we present the first nucl
papers.summary: This study presents the first haplotype-resolved, chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for Carya glabra (pignut hickory), a tetraploid species in the walnut family. The new genomic resource will facilitate studies of evolutionary history and biology in hickories, with potential applications for improving the closely related pecan crop.

papers.title: Association of IL-8 and IL-18 Expression With Histone-Associated NETosis in Aqueous-Deficient and Evaporative Dry Eye Disease.
papers.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the ocular surface; however, upstream immune mechanisms contributing to DED are complex and unclear. This study aimed to identify differentially expressed tear proteins in patients with DED and elucidate the underlying disease mechanism.
papers.summary: This study identifies differentially expressed tear proteins in dry eye disease (DED) patients, focusing on IL-8 and IL-18, and links their expression to histone-associated NETosis (a form of neutrophil cell death) in both aqueous-deficient and evaporative DED subtypes. The findings suggest that NETosis-related inflammation may be a key upstream mechanism in DED pathogenesis.

papers.title: Integrating short-read and long-read single-cell transcriptomics of pig pituitary reveals mechanisms of high-altitude hypoxia adaptation.
papers.abstract: Acting as the central endocrine hub, the pituitary gland is closely related to the mechanism of adaptation to high-altitude hypoxia. Here, by integratively combining long-read (Oxford Nanopore) and short-read (Illumina) single-cell sequencing approaches, we profiled pituitaries from Diqing Tibetan pigs, inhabiting high-altitude environments (3,200 m) and Diannan small-ear pigs from low-altitude regions (500 m), thereby generating a full-length single-cell atlas, which in turn enabled the identification of molecular mechanisms potentially underlying adaptation to high-altitude hypoxia stress. S
papers.summary: This study integrates long-read and short-read single-cell transcriptomics to profile pituitary glands from high-altitude Tibetan pigs and low-altitude pigs, generating a full-length single-cell atlas. The analysis identifies molecular mechanisms potentially underlying adaptation to high-altitude hypoxia stress.

papers.title: IP-LC-MS/MS-Based Identification of Candidate TPL2 (MAP3K8)-Associated Proteins in Porcine PK-15 Cells.
papers.abstract: Tumor progression locus 2 (TPL2, also known as MAP-3K8/COT) is a kinase that regulates MAPK and NF-κB signaling and contributes to antiviral immunity. While mammalian TPL2 has been widely studied, the TPL2-associated protein profile in swine cells remains largely unexplored. In this study, we generated an IP-LC-MS/MS-based candidate dataset of TPL2-associated proteins in porcine kidney epithelial (PK-15) cells. FLAG-tagged TPL2 was overexpressed in PK-15 cells and enriched by immunoprecipitation, followed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis. After subtraction
papers.summary: This study generated a candidate dataset of TPL2-associated proteins in porcine PK-15 cells using immunoprecipitation followed by LC-MS/MS, identifying potential interaction partners of this kinase involved in antiviral immunity. The findings provide a resource for studying TPL2 signaling in swine and may inform veterinary vaccine development.

papers.title: Nigericin-Triggered Phosphodynamics in Inflammasome Formation and Pyroptosis.
papers.abstract: Innate immune signaling relies heavily on phosphorylation cascades to mount effective immune responses. Although traditional innate immune signaling cascades following TLR4 stimulation have been investigated through a temporally quantitative phosphoproteomic lens, far fewer studies have applied these methods to distinct signaling following the inflammasome trigger leading to IL-1β release. Here, we conducted time-resolved phosphoproteomic profiling to investigate kinase signaling downstream of the inflammasome trigger nigericin. We found that nigericin induces rapid and potent alterations in t
papers.summary: This study uses time-resolved phosphoproteomics to map kinase signaling downstream of the inflammasome trigger nigericin, revealing rapid and potent phosphorylation changes that drive inflammasome formation and pyroptosis. It provides a new resource for understanding innate immune signaling beyond TLR4 pathways.

papers.title: De novo whole transcriptome sequencing reveals differentially expressed messenger RNA and MicroRNA in hepatopancreas of Pandalus hypsinotus.
papers.abstract: Pandalus hypsinotus (P. hypsinotus), also known as coonstripe shrimp, has high economic value and is widely distributed in Alaska, the Bering Sea and the East Sea of Korea. However, owing to the low catch rates and patchy spatial distribution, transcriptome-based studies on this species remain limited. Transcriptome analyses using PacBio Iso-Seq and Illumina RNA sequencing techniques were performed to establish a de novo unigene set of P. hypsinotus and identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the hepatopancreas compared to the tail muscle. A search of all the unigenes against Gene On
papers.summary: This study generated a de novo transcriptome for the coonstripe shrimp (Pandalus hypsinotus) using PacBio and Illumina sequencing, identifying differentially expressed mRNAs and microRNAs in the hepatopancreas versus tail muscle. The work provides a valuable genomic resource for this economically important but understudied species, with potential applications in aquaculture and molecular ecology.

papers.title: Leveraging expression quantitative trait loci information in single-cell resolution to identify cell-specific genes for Basal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC), the most common skin cancer, is driven by UV-induced DNA damage and shaped by immune surveillance. Although GWAS has identified over 140 risk loci, their cell-type-specific effects remain obscured by tissue-level averaging.
papers.summary: This study integrates expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data with single-cell RNA sequencing to identify cell-type-specific genes associated with basal cell carcinoma (BCC) risk, overcoming the limitations of tissue-level averaging in GWAS. The approach reveals immune and stromal cell-specific gene expression changes linked to BCC susceptibility, providing new insights into the cellular mechanisms underlying this common skin cancer.
